newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-DUTCH HAVE LONG HISTORY OF SOCCER VIOLENCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DUTCH HAVE LONG HISTORY OF SOCCER VIOLENCE.

text.p: The death of an Ajax Amsterdam fan in a pre-arranged battle between soccer supporters on Sunday is the latest in a long chronicle of football violence in the Netherlands.
This is a chronology since the 1970s.
1974 - Feyenoord and Tottenham Hotspur fans riot during UEFA Cup final in Rotterdam.
Sept 28, 1986 - 72 Feyenoord fans arrested after violent clashes during league match against PSV Eindhoven.
October 1986 - Police open national file of known soccer hooligans, estimating a hard-core of 2,000.
Oct 22, 1986 - Police arrest 71 Feyenoord fans after rioting at UEFA Cup game against Borussia Moenchengladbach in Germany.
March 1, 1987 - Den Haag versus Ajax Amsterdam league game abandoned after crowd violence.

October 1987 - International between Netherlands and Cyprus in Rotterdam halted for one hour after visiting goalkeeper hit by home-made bomb thrown from the stands. UEFA banned the Rotterdam stadium from hosting European matches.
Dec 18, 1988 - Police crackdown nets 82 Ajax Amsterdam fans travelling to league game against Willem II of Tilburg.
1989 - Dutch soccer authorities introduce experimental identity card system. Total soccer-related arrests reach almost 1,000 in 1988/89 season.
April 27, 1989 - Ugly street clashes between Dutch and West German fans in Rotterdam ahead of World Cup qualifying match. 70 arrests. 40 fans and three police injured.
Sept 8, 1989 - Dutch and English soccer authorities cancel friendly international in Rotterdam for fear of hooliganism.
Sept 27, 1989 - Ajax fans throw iron bars onto pitch during UEFA Cup tie between Ajax and Austria Vienna, injuring Vienna goalkeeper. UEFA bans Ajax from European competition for a year.
Oct 20, 1989 - Feyenoord ordered to play league game behind closed doors as punishment for pitch invasion in August league game versus Fortuna Sittard.
Oct 21, 1989 - 14 injured after Feyenoord fans hurl bombs at Ajax supporters during league game in Amsterdam. Five arrests.
Jan 10, 1990 - Den Haag fined and ordered to play behind closed doors after fans hurl stones on pitch during league game.
March 22, 1990 - Police arrest 42 Dutch and German fans ahead of PSV Eindhoven versus Bayern Munich European Cup tie in Eindhoven.
March 24, 1990 - Groningen fans rampage on train before league game in Tilburg. 36 arrested.
May 6, 1990 - Riot police arrest 28 Ajax fans ahead of league game in Nijmegen.
Sept 9, 1990 - 50 Feyenoord fans arrested after explosive device thrown from train, injuring an elderly man.
Jan 13, 1995 - Crowd violence halts league match between Ajax Amsterdam and RKC Waalwijk. Match official injured by missile.
March 7, 1996 - Over 100 Dutch and German fans clash before European Cup Winners Cup tie between Feyenoord and Borussia Moenchengladbach in Duesseldorf. 18 arrests.
April 25, 1996 - Police arrest 71 Dutch and German fans at friendly international in Rotterdam.

Nov 24, 1996 - A dozen arrests at Feyenoord-Ajax league match in Rotterdam, dubbed by Dutch media as "The Match of Hate". Fans lobbed fire-bomb and pelted police with ball bearings. Ajax team coach was stoned.
Dec 14, 1996 - Police arrest 123 Dutch and Belgian fans before a World Cup qualifying match in Brussels.
Feb 16, 1997 - Around 80 Ajax and Feyenoord fans brandishing variety of weapons clash on ring road near Amsterdam. No injuries or arrests.
Feb 24, 1997 - Police postpone Sparta Rotterdam versus Ajax Amsterdam league match due to fears of violence between Ajax and Feyenoord fans
